title: Encode and Decode Strings
prompt:
Design an algorithm to **encode** a list of strings into one string, and **decode** it back to the original list. The strings can contain ANY characters (commas, `#`, spaces, empty strings) — so a naive `join(",")` won't work.

To make this testable here, implement two private helpers `encode(List<String>)` and `decode(String)`, and the graded method returns `decode(encode(strs))` — it must reproduce the input exactly.

The classic scheme: prefix each string with its length and a delimiter, e.g. `"5#hello3#foo"`.

tests.note: delimiter and digits inside the data

hints: Encode each string as `<length>#<string>`. The length tells the decoder exactly how many chars to read, so the content can contain anything.
Decode: read digits until `#` to get the length, then take exactly that many characters as the string, and continue.
Track an index `i` through the encoded string; after reading one chunk, jump `i` past it.

solution.explanation: Length-prefixing is delimiter-proof: because the decoder reads a fixed count of characters, the payload can legally contain `#`, digits, commas, or be empty. This same framing ("length then bytes") is how real network protocols avoid ambiguity.
